prompt: Complete BufferedStreamRelay.relay so it copies an InputStream into an OutputStream using a byte buffer of the given size and returns the number of bytes copied.
explanation: InputStream.read(byte[]) fills as much of the buffer as it can and returns the count actually read, which is often less than the buffer length even when more data is coming -- only -1 means end of stream. Writing out.write(buffer) instead of out.write(buffer, 0, count) is the classic bug: it writes stale bytes left in the buffer from the previous read. Buffering this way turns thousands of one-byte system calls into a handful of larger ones.
hints: Declare the buffer once outside the loop and reuse it for every read.
Store the result of in.read(buffer) in an int and loop while it is not -1.
Always write with the three-argument out.write(buffer, 0, count) so you never write leftover bytes.
